title: Filtered continuity of internal derived invariants for a profinite group
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group. Write $\mathcal A_J(R)$ for internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an $R$-linear action of $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and $\Gamma_{R,J}$ for the submodule fixed after every profinite base change. Use its ordinary total right derived functor [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], and put $R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N)=H^q(R\Gamma_{R,J}(N[0]))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every small filtered category $I$ (nonempty, with a common target for every finite diagram) and diagram $(N_i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal A_J(R)$, forgetting the action creates its filtered colimit: its underlying module is the sheaf colimit, with the induced action. For every $q\geq0$ the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i)\longrightarrow R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}N_i)$$
is an isomorphism of internal $R$-modules. The legs are exactly the maps induced by the original colimit coprojections. All indexing categories, profinite parameters and sheaves lie in the chosen compatible universes. No discreteness, finite generation, norm completeness, or bounded cohomological dimension is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-action-filtered-colimit-creation] to the given diagram. It constructs the equivariant colimit $L$ on the underlying sheaf colimit, with the original coprojections $\iota_i$, and so proves the creation clause. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-action-colimit-cohomology] to this colimit cocone $(L,\iota_i)$. For $F_i=\Phi(N_i)$ and $F=\Phi(L)$ it gives the presheaf isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_iP_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, where $P_i(S)=H^q(tS,(F_i)_{ab})$ and $P(S)=H^q(tS,F_{ab})$. Its $i$-leg is the coefficient map induced by $\Phi(\iota_i)$; restriction compatibility is part of the cited statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-invariants-sheafified-cohomology] to every $N_i$ and to $L$. Its natural isomorphisms identify $P_i^\#$ with $U(R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i))$ and $P^\#$ with $U(R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(L))$. Its displayed naturality equation for $\iota_i$ identifies each sheafified coefficient leg with $U(R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(\iota_i))$. Thus the comparison retains the original coprojections, rather than merely giving unrelated object isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images, injective-resolution sheafification argument, with the agent-formulated normalized action-module and underlying-abelian acyclic comparison. Blueprint main-20261015, direct-images proof paragraph (3), relative comparison needed for filtered internal invariants.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], sheafification commutes with colimits. Write $c:\operatorname{colim}_iP_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ for step 1. With the natural comparisons of step 2, the resulting abelian-sheaf isomorphism is $\beta=\alpha_L^q\circ c^\#\circ(\operatorname{colim}_i\alpha_{N_i}^q)^{-1}$. For the coprojection $j_i$ into $\operatorname{colim}_iU(R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i))$, the leg identity of $c$ and the naturality equation of $\alpha$ give $\beta\circ j_i=U(R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(\iota_i))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], this source is the underlying abelian sheaf of the internal module colimit. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], higher invariants take values in internal modules. Their canonical linear comparison $f$ has precisely these legs; the colimit universal property therefore gives $U(f)=\beta$. Its inverse is linear: applying the injective linear $f$ to $f^{-1}(ry)=rf^{-1}(y)$ gives equality. Thus $f$ is an internal-module isomorphism for every $q\geq0$, with the original coprojections and no uniform bound in $q$.
